title: Ninth Word Fifth Point Night Prayer And The Transformations Of The Universe

questions.question: What happens in the sky at the time of 'Isha in this passage?
questions.answer: The last light of day disappears, and night covers the world.

questions.question: What does the passing of time do to the works left behind by those who are gone?
questions.answer: It removes their traces from this world.

questions.question: What bigger truth does that fading away remind people of?
questions.answer: It reminds them that living things pass from this world into another world.

questions.question: How is this world described when it is compared with the hereafter?
questions.answer: This world is shown as small, temporary, and low, while the hereafter is wide, lasting, and majestic.

questions.question: Who alone deserves to own, manage, love, and be worshipped in the universe?
questions.answer: Allah alone deserves that.

questions.question: Why does the passage say only Allah can be the true object of worship?
questions.answer: Because He easily changes huge things, like night and day, winter and spring, and this world and the next.

questions.question: What picture is used to show how easily Allah changes things?
questions.answer: The passage says it is like turning the pages of a book.

questions.question: What two actions with the pages of a book are compared to Allah’s power over creation?
questions.answer: Writing and erasing.

questions.question: What main lesson about 'Isha does this part teach?
questions.answer: It teaches that 'Isha is a time to remember Allah’s power, the passing of this world, and the reality of the hereafter.

questions.question: At nightfall, what disappears from the horizon?
questions.answer: The last signs of daytime disappear.

questions.question: After the day ends, what fills the universe?
questions.answer: The world of night spreads over it.

questions.question: Which seasonal change is mentioned along with the change from day to night?
questions.answer: The change from summer to winter.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention old traces being wiped away over time?
questions.answer: To show that things in this world do not stay forever.

questions.question: What does this teach about life in this world?
questions.answer: It teaches that this life is temporary and leads to another life.

questions.question: What event connected to this world is described in a very serious and frightening way?
questions.answer: The end of this world is described as a terrible dying.

questions.question: What appears after the destruction of this passing world?
questions.answer: The great and everlasting world of the hereafter appears.

questions.question: What does the passage say about Allah’s ability to make changes?
questions.answer: It says He makes great changes with ease.

questions.question: Name one pair of opposites in the passage that Allah changes into each other.
questions.answer: Night and day.

questions.question: If Allah can make all these changes, what should a believer understand about Him?
questions.answer: A believer should understand that Allah has complete power and alone deserves worship.

questions.question: What time of day is the target passage about?
questions.answer: It is about the time of 'Isha, at nightfall.

questions.question: What natural change begins this passage?
questions.answer: Daylight fades away and night takes over.

questions.question: How does the passage help us think about Allah’s control of the world?
questions.answer: It points to the changes Allah brings in time, seasons, life, and worlds.

questions.question: What season is described as green and decorated?
questions.answer: Summer.

questions.question: What season is described as cold and white?
questions.answer: Winter.

questions.question: What happens to the marks left by people after they are gone?
questions.answer: They slowly disappear from this world.

questions.question: What does that disappearing suggest about the people and things of this life?
questions.answer: It suggests they do not remain here forever.

questions.question: How is the hereafter different from this world in the passage?
questions.answer: The hereafter is described as broad, eternal, and glorious, unlike this brief world.

questions.question: According to the passage, who is the true manager of the universe?
questions.answer: Allah is the true manager of the universe.

questions.question: What does the coming of night remind a person of in this passage?
questions.answer: It reminds a person of Allah’s power and of bigger changes in creation.

questions.question: Which daily change is mentioned first as a sign of Allah’s power?
questions.answer: The change from day to night.

questions.question: Which yearly change is mentioned next?
questions.answer: The change from summer to winter.

questions.question: Which change in the unseen future is mentioned after those?
questions.answer: The movement from this world to another world.

questions.question: Why are these three changes important in the passage?
questions.answer: They show that Allah controls everything from small daily changes to the biggest changes of existence.

questions.question: How is this present world described?
questions.answer: It is described as narrow, passing, and low.

questions.question: How is the world to come described?
questions.answer: It is described as vast, everlasting, and majestic.

questions.question: What example helps readers understand how easy these changes are for Allah?
questions.answer: They are compared to turning pages in a book.

questions.question: Besides turning pages, what else is mentioned in that book example?
questions.answer: Writing on the pages and wiping things from them.

questions.question: In the passage, what happens when the last brightness of day is gone?
questions.answer: Night spreads over everything.

questions.question: Who is shown as the One bringing this change?
questions.answer: Allah is shown as the One bringing it.

questions.question: What happens to the signs of people’s work after they leave this world?
questions.answer: Those signs fade away as time passes.

questions.question: What can a reader infer from that fading away?
questions.answer: A reader can infer that worldly things do not last.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the end of this world?
questions.answer: It describes the world as coming to an end in a fearful way.

questions.question: What follows after the end of this temporary world?
questions.answer: The hereafter, which lasts forever, comes forward.

questions.question: Why does the passage reject taking anything other than Allah as the true beloved and object of worship?
questions.answer: Because only Allah has the power to control all these great changes.

questions.question: Which examples in the passage show Allah’s complete power over time and existence?
questions.answer: Changing night and day, winter and spring, and this world and the hereafter.

questions.question: What is the best summary of this whole passage?
questions.answer: 'Isha time teaches that Allah alone controls all changes and that this world passes away while the hereafter remains.

questions.question: What is the first scene described in this passage about 'Isha?
questions.answer: The final light of day disappears and night takes over.

questions.question: What does this scene teach about Allah?
questions.answer: It teaches that Allah controls the changes of the universe.

questions.question: Which change of seasons is used as another example of His power?
questions.answer: The shift from summer to winter.

questions.question: How does the passage connect time passing with human life?
questions.answer: It says that as time passes, what people leave behind in the world is erased.

questions.question: What does that erasing remind us of beyond this life?
questions.answer: It reminds us of moving on to another world.

questions.question: How does the passage describe this world compared with what comes after?
questions.answer: This world is temporary and limited, but what comes after is lasting and great.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the One who truly runs the universe?
questions.answer: It says the true ruler and caretaker is Allah alone.

questions.question: What comparison is made to show how easily Allah changes things?
questions.answer: His changing of worlds is compared to handling book pages.

questions.question: What three major changes are listed near the end of the passage?
questions.answer: Night becoming day, winter becoming spring, and this world becoming the hereafter.

questions.question: How should this passage shape a Muslim student’s understanding of worship?
questions.answer: It should help the student see that worship belongs only to Allah, who has power over everything and whose hereafter is everlasting.
